AEGIS TITAN — RESEARCH / ARCHITECTURE REFERENCE
================================================================================

Page 1 - TITLE
PROJECT AEGIS TITAN
A Multi-Agent Edge Artificial Intelligence Framework for Secure Autonomous Device Management.
Research fields: AI, Edge Computing, Cybersecurity, Mobile Systems.
Researcher: Ntsakiso Vutlhari Chauke.
Page 2 - ABSTRACT
AI assistants usually depend on cloud computing... AEGIS TITAN investigates an edge-based AI assistant that learns, protects privacy, helps with school, work and coding while operating mainly on-device.
Page 3 - BACKGROUND
Most AI systems rely on cloud servers causing latency and privacy concerns. Edge AI processes data locally for faster and safer performance.
Page 4 - PROBLEM STATEMENT
Cloud AI depends on internet, increases latency and privacy risks, and has limited hardware control.
Page 5 - AIM
The aim is to design an Android AI assistant that learns continuously, protects privacy, improves cybersecurity, teaches users, writes code and adapts over time.
Page 6 - RESEARCH QUESTION
Can an edge-based multi-agent AI framework provide faster, safer and more personalized smartphone assistance than cloud AI?
Page 7 - HYPOTHESIS
If AI is distributed across local software agents, response time, privacy, personalization and cybersecurity will improve.
Page 8 - OBJECTIVES
Develop Kotlin-Python framework; build multi-agent AI; adaptive memory; AI clone; coding assistant; evaluate cybersecurity and performance.
Page 9 - LITERATURE REVIEW
Edge AI, local language models and multi-agent systems are emerging technologies that improve responsiveness, privacy and autonomous decision making.
Page 10 - SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE
Main modules: EDITH (coordination), Omega Brain (reasoning), Omega Forge (learning), Memory Vault (memory), AI Clone (personalization), Cybersecurity.
Page 11 - METHODOLOGY
Design architecture, develop app, integrate AI, test cybersecurity, perform experiments, collect data and analyse results.
Page 12 - FEATURES OF AEGIS TITAN
Offline AI, voice assistant, adaptive learning, AI tutor, coding assistant, task management, automation, encrypted memory, AI clone.
Page 13 - CYBERSECURITY
Uses encryption, authentication, behaviour monitoring and secure storage to protect personal information and detect threats.
Page 14 - AI LEARNING SYSTEM
Learns from YouTube, websites, PDFs, GitHub and documents. Stores knowledge in Memory Vault for future use.
Page 15 - AI CLONE
Learns the user's communication style, interests, goals and preferences to provide personalized responses.
Page 16 - CODING ASSISTANT
Writes Kotlin and Python code, explains programming concepts, fixes bugs and teaches coding step by step.
Page 17 - EXPECTED RESULTS
Expected improvements include lower latency, better privacy, improved coding assistance and personalized learning.
Page 18 - DATA COLLECTION
Collect latency, CPU, RAM, battery, task success, learning accuracy, security detection rate and stability metrics.
Page 19 - CONCLUSION
AEGIS TITAN demonstrates how Edge AI can combine learning, cybersecurity and intelligent assistance into one mobile platform.
Page 20 - FUTURE WORK
Future work includes robotics, IoT, smart homes, drones, healthcare, federated learning and energy-efficient AI.
Page 21 - REFERENCES
References: Android Developers, Kotlin Docs, Python Docs, MediaPipe, OpenAI, Whisper, Ollama and Edge AI research.

StudyLock_Complete_Project_Overview_2026.text:
STUDYLOCK — COMPLETE PROJECT OVERVIEW, BUILD HISTORY, FEATURES, ERRORS, AND CURRENT STATUS
========================================================================================

Document date: 22 September 2026
Project: StudyLock
Organization: Cyber Pulse
Primary purpose: Study/focus control, distraction blocking, learning support, family/teacher supervision, offline learning, and protected study sessions.

IMPORTANT STATUS NOTE
---------------------
This document reconstructs the StudyLock project from the recorded project history through 22 September 2026.
It includes implemented features, requested features, experimental builds, known errors, fixes attempted, and items that still need real-device verification.
Where a feature was requested or attempted but was not fully proven on a real device, it is clearly marked as such.

================================================================================
1. WHAT STUDYLOCK IS
================================================================================

StudyLock is a connected education and focus-control ecosystem designed to help a student study without distractions while giving approved parents and teachers controlled ways to support the student.

The project grew from a single student focus app into a multi-app system made of:

1. StudyLock Student
2. StudyLock Parent
3. StudyLock Teacher
4. StudyLock Parent HTML Dashboard
5. Earlier desktop/Windows StudyLock experiments
6. Shared Firebase / connected-system infrastructure
7. Offline learning libraries and imported knowledge packs

The main goals of StudyLock are:

- Keep the student focused during study sessions.
- Block selected distracting apps.
- Prevent a student from casually disabling protection during an active session.
- Provide an AI Tutor.
- Work as much as possible without internet.
- Allow the Parent app to pair with the Student app.
- Allow the Parent app to remotely start or manage study controls.
- Allow the Teacher app to share school content with students.
- Track study time, focus state, AI usage, blocked apps, schedules, goals, and other learning information.
- Provide quizzes, notes, planning, progress tracking, rewards, learning resources, and study tools.
- Use a recognizable StudyLock liquid/glass-style interface.
- Keep Student, Parent, and Teacher as separate applications while allowing them to communicate.

================================================================================
2. MAIN STUDYLOCK APPLICATIONS
================================================================================

STUDYLOCK STUDENT
-----------------

Package:
com.studylock.student

The Student app is the main StudyLock application installed on the learner's device.

Its responsibilities include:

- Study/focus sessions.
- App blocking.
- Focus timers.
- Auto Study.
- Study schedules.
- AI Tutor.
- Offline Tutor fallback.
- Quiz system.
- Offline quizzes.
- Notes.
- Planner.
- Progress tracking.
- Learning resources.
- Rewards / XP concepts.
- Library import.
- Local learning databases.
- Study statistics.
- Parent pairing.
- Teacher joining.
- Parent commands.
- Teacher content delivery.
- PIN-protected settings.
- Device Admin / protection features.
- Accessibility-based app blocking.
- Student status reporting.
- Focus heartbeat / connection status.

The Student app has generally been treated as the visual and functional reference app for the Parent and Teacher versions.

STUDYLOCK PARENT
----------------

Package:
com.studylock.parent

The Parent app is intended to pair with one or more Student installations and provide parental control over StudyLock functions.

Main Parent functions include:

- Generate a pairing code.
- Show a pairing code.
- QR-based pairing.
- Link to a Student app.
- View the student's focus state.
- View study metrics.
- View study time.
- View blocked apps.
- View AI usage statistics.
- Start a study/focus session remotely.
- End a session when authorized.
- Configure or send schedules.
- Control Auto Study.
- Set or refresh protection-related controls.
- Receive approval requests.
- Manage goals and assignments in later connected-system designs.
- Monitor connection / heartbeat state.

The Parent app has gone through several different implementations because its pairing behavior was one of the largest problem areas in the project.

STUDYLOCK TEACHER
-----------------

Package:
com.studylock.teacher

The Teacher app is intended for academic communication rather than parental device-security control.

Teacher functionality has included or been requested to include:

- Create or join a class structure.
- Generate or use class/join codes.
- Connect students to a teacher.
- Send notes.
- Send announcements.
- Send assignments.
- Send learning resources.
- Send questions.
- Share commitments / tasks.
- Broadcast content to all students.
- Group communication concepts.
- Share whiteboard snapshots in later connected builds.
- Maintain teacher/student heartbeat or presence.

Important design rule:
The Teacher app should not have the same security authority as the Parent app. Teacher functions are focused on learning, classes, assignments, resources, and communication.

PARENT HTML DASHBOARD
---------------------

The Parent HTML dashboard became an important diagnostic reference because, at different points, it connected successfully to the Student app while the Parent APK did not.

Known Parent HTML filenames have included versions such as:

- studylock-parent-dashboard-1-2.html
- studylock-parent-dashboard-1-2(2).html
- studylock-parent-dashboard-1-2(3).html
- studylock-parent-dashboard-1-3.html

A major investigation in September 2026 focused on understanding why this HTML dashboard could connect while the Android Parent APK failed.

At least one recorded HTML implementation used a different communication approach, including ntfy.sh/localStorage behavior, while the Android Parent app was expected to use Firebase/Firestore. This difference is important because two interfaces that look similar can still use completely different networking and pairing logic.

================================================================================
3. STUDYLOCK VISUAL DESIGN
================================================================================

StudyLock's visual identity has changed across versions, but several strong design directions became consistent.

STUDENT DESIGN
--------------

The Student app became the main design reference.

Important style elements:

- Liquid-glass / liquid-style controls.
- Orange or yellow/orange StudyLock accent.
- Rounded cards.
- Modern mobile dashboard.
- Smooth visual hierarchy.
- Focus-centered interface.
- Darker or glass-like sections in later builds.
- Existing Student design should be preserved when repairing connectivity.

PARENT AND TEACHER DESIGN
-------------------------

The Parent and Teacher applications were later required to move away from plain or white backgrounds.

The requested direction became:

- Use the Student app as the UI/UX reference.
- Use the same yellowish / liquid yellow or orange visual identity.
- Avoid white background-heavy screens.
- Prefer dark backgrounds.
- Blue/cyan or purple supporting tones were also requested in some repair iterations.
- Use liquid-orange / liquid-yellow controls.
- Preserve pairing, QR, Firebase, and control functionality while changing the appearance.

The goal is for all three applications to feel like one StudyLock family rather than unrelated apps.

================================================================================
4. EARLY STUDYLOCK / HTML-TO-ANDROID PHASE
================================================================================

An important early StudyLock goal was to reproduce an existing StudyLock HTML interface as a real Android application.

The HTML reference included major screens such as:

- Focus
- Planner
- Tutor
- Quiz
- Notes
- Progress
- Learn
- Rewards
- Authentication / onboarding
- Settings
- History
- Background music
- App blocking controls

An Android rebuild was created around the idea of preserving the HTML look while adding native Android capabilities.

Native additions included or were planned to include:

- Accessibility-based app blocking.
- Android notifications.
- Speech input.
- Text-to-speech.
- Camera/file access.
- Persistent app state.
- Settings PIN.
- Block list.
- XP / reward state.
- Focus session enforcement.

One early build was referred to as:
StudyLock-Individual-Rebuilt.apk

The native app blocker required Android Accessibility permission to be enabled.

A limitation noted in early builds was that blocking websites inside a web browser was different from blocking Android apps and remained a separate problem.

================================================================================
5. FAMILY EDITION PHASE
================================================================================

StudyLock later expanded into a Student/Parent connected system.

At one point, the project structure used modules similar to:

- :student
- :parent
- :shared

A backend/project name used in the StudyLock family work was:
studylock-family

The system was designed so the Student and Parent applications used the same backend/Firebase project.

Parent/Student functions included:

- 6-digit pairing.
- QR pairing.
- Live focus status.
- Study statistics.
- Remote Auto Study control.
- Remote Start Study.
- Authorized End Study.
- Scheduled study.
- Duration options including 25, 45, 60, and 90 minutes in one control-center version.
- Blocked-app visibility.
- Student metrics.
- Daily start behavior.

One implementation used a FastAPI server in a desktop-family experiment.

The Android family system later focused much more heavily on Firebase/Firestore.

================================================================================
6. ANDROID BUILD TECHNOLOGY
================================================================================

StudyLock Android development has primarily used:

- Kotlin
- Android Studio
- Jetpack Compose in native versions
- Gradle
- Firebase
- Firestore
- Firebase Authentication in some versions
- Google Services configuration
- Android Accessibility Service
- Device Admin APIs
- WebView/native bridge concepts in HTML-based builds
- Local databases / packaged learning assets
- Offline import logic

- compileSdk: 35
- minSdk: 26

StudyLock pairing has used several approaches over its development.

PAIRING METHODS
---------------

  studylock://pair

----------------------

A repeated issue was that the Parent "Generate new key" or pairing-code button did not work correctly in some APK builds.

---------------

However, Firebase and LAN are different systems:
- Firebase can synchronize across different networks if internet and backend configuration work.
- LAN can work between devices on the same local network if the apps implement direct local networking correctly.

Having both phones on the same Wi-Fi does not automatically make two StudyLock APKs connect unless the APKs actually contain the same LAN protocol, ports, discovery method, permissions, and message format.

- Parent app expecting the Student to respond through a different transport.
- Student waiting for a dashboard heartbeat that the Parent APK never sends.

16. DEVICE ADMIN, PIN, AND UNINSTALL PROTECTION
================================================================================

One of the most important StudyLock security requirements is that the student should not be able to disable protection without authorization.

PIN
---

A 6-digit PIN has been used for:
- First launch.
- Settings protection.
- Admin deactivation approval.
- Uninstall-release concept.
- Parent/security controls.

The desired behavior:

1. First launch asks for or creates the 6-digit PIN.
2. StudyLock is granted the required admin/accessibility permissions.
3. The user cannot simply enter settings and disable the protection without the PIN.
4. Uninstall should require an authorized release process.

REPORTED PROBLEM
----------------

The user repeatedly reported that StudyLock could still be uninstalled because Android allowed Device Admin to be deactivated without StudyLock successfully forcing a PIN first.

This is a platform-level issue as well as an implementation issue.

Classic Device Admin does not give a normal third-party Android application absolute control over Settings or the package installer.

TRUE STRONGER LOCKDOWN
----------------------

For significantly stronger uninstall prevention, Android Device Owner / managed-device deployment is generally required.

Some StudyLock native v5 work referred to:
- Device Owner
- Lock Task

But a consumer-installed APK cannot silently make itself Device Owner on an already configured phone.

Therefore, "PIN before uninstall" can be approximated in a normal app, but cannot be guaranteed against the actual device owner unless the device is enrolled/managed in a supported Android management mode.

================================================================================
50. STUDYLOCK CORE PRINCIPLES
================================================================================

The finished StudyLock system should follow these principles:

1. STUDY FIRST
The core purpose is to improve focus and learning, not just monitor the student.

2. OFFLINE CAPABLE
The Student should retain meaningful learning functions without internet.

3. CONNECTED WHEN AVAILABLE
Parent and Teacher controls should synchronize reliably when connectivity is available.

4. CLEAR AUTHORITY
Parent controls security/focus.
Teacher controls learning/class content.
Student retains the main learning interface.

5. PRIVACY
Do not turn StudyLock into secret message surveillance.

6. HARD TO BYPASS, BUT HONEST ABOUT ANDROID LIMITS
Use PIN, Accessibility, Device Admin, and managed-device features correctly without falsely claiming a normal APK can become impossible to uninstall.

7. ONE DESIGN FAMILY
Student, Parent, and Teacher should clearly look like StudyLock.

8. RELIABLE BUILDS
Every release APK must be:
- parseable
- signed
- installable
- correctly versioned
- tested

9. REAL TESTING
A successful Gradle build is not enough.
Pairing, blocking, security, offline behavior, and syncing must be tested on physical Android devices.

10. SEPARATE APPS, SHARED SYSTEM
Student, Parent, and Teacher remain separate APKs but share a common protocol and backend schema.

================================================================================
51. SIMPLE DESCRIPTION OF STUDYLOCK
================================================================================

StudyLock is a Cyber Pulse learning and focus ecosystem made of Student, Parent, and Teacher apps.

The Student app helps a learner focus, blocks distracting apps, runs protected study sessions, provides quizzes, notes, planning, progress tools, learning libraries, and an AI Tutor that can use both online and offline information.

The Parent app pairs with the Student app using a code or QR and is designed to view study information, manage schedules, control Auto Study, start or authorize focus sessions, and manage protection-related settings.

The Teacher app connects to students for academic purposes such as sending notes, assignments, questions, resources, announcements, and visual/class content.

The system has evolved through many Android, HTML, Firebase, offline-library, and security builds. Its biggest technical challenges have been reliable Parent/Student/Teacher synchronization, Firebase configuration, APK signing/install compatibility, offline learning databases, and Android's limitations around uninstall prevention.

The current direction is to keep all three apps separate, make them share one reliable communication protocol, preserve the Student app's features, redesign Parent and Teacher to match the Student's liquid yellow/orange visual language, and verify every feature on real devices.

END OF STUDYLOCK PROJECT RECORD

STUDYOS — COMPLETE PROJECT KNOWLEDGE RECORD
================================================================================
Document date: 22 September 2026
Project family: Cyber Pulse education / AI operating-environment work
Primary documented builder / architect: Ntsakiso Chauke / DARTHWOLF

STATUS AND INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
This record combines the confirmed StudyOS direction with historical/experimental concepts discussed during its evolution. Ember must distinguish a design target or experiment from a verified shipped feature. Do not claim a feature is running on a real device unless the current project evidence confirms that.

1. WHAT STUDYOS IS
------------------
StudyOS is a student-focused operating environment intended to combine learning, AI tutoring, productivity, local/offline intelligence, voice, device integration, and study workflows into one system. It is broader than a normal study app: its direction is an AI-first student operating environment that can continue to function when cloud services or internet access are unavailable.

StudyOS is not the same project as StudyLock, Study AI, Star AI, AEGIS, or Infinity OS.
- StudyLock: focus control, app blocking, Student/Parent/Teacher ecosystem.
- Study AI: education-focused AI tutor/assistant.
- StudyOS: broader student AI operating environment/platform.
- Star AI: general-purpose assistant.
- AEGIS / Infinity OS: later/broader AI-computing and device-control directions.

Historical lineage discussed:
Evolution Learning -> StudyOS -> AEGIS -> Infinity OS
This is a development/influence lineage, not a claim that all four are the same product.

2. STUDYOS V4.0 DIRECTION
-------------------------
StudyOS v4.0 was defined around offline-first local AI.
Core direction:
- Offline-first operation.
- Local language models.
- llama.cpp-based local inference concepts.
- Whisper.cpp-based local speech recognition concepts.
- Local speech / voice interaction.
- Minimal dependence on permanent cloud connectivity.
- Student-centered AI and learning workflows.
- Local knowledge and retrieval.

Local model examples associated with v4:
- Phi-3 Mini class, including the 3.8B-class direction.
- Gemma 2 2B class.
These are model directions/targets and should not be described as permanently bundled unless the actual build contains them.

Historical/experimental v4 architecture ideas also included:
- Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over local study knowledge.
- Local vector/search memory concepts.
- LoRA / PEFT-style adaptation ideas for specialized learning behavior.
- Dedicated task agents for areas such as homework, research, coding, and tutoring.
- Local/REST control interfaces and LAN-based communication experiments.
- Separation of student data, local knowledge, model runtime, and task-agent layers.

3. STUDYOS V5.0 DIRECTION
-------------------------
StudyOS v5.0 expanded the concept beyond a single phone application.
Target platforms/directions:
- Android.
- Wear OS.
- Embedded-device concepts.

Core v5 ideas:
- Encrypted local models / protected model storage.
- No-cloud or cloud-optional operating mode.
- Wear OS tiles / quick study controls.
- A remote-brain concept over local networks (LAN), allowing a stronger nearby device to perform heavier processing for a smaller device.
- Agent-swarm / multi-agent study intelligence.
- Distributed study intelligence across permitted devices.
- Stronger owner-controlled trust boundaries for connected devices.
- Encrypted Device Mesh concepts in later/stricter designs.

The owner-only / encrypted Device Mesh direction should be treated as an access-control goal: only explicitly authorized devices/users should participate. It is not permission to bypass device security or account controls.

4. OFFLINE AI PHILOSOPHY
------------------------
StudyOS repeatedly emphasizes offline capability because student access to stable internet, data, or cloud providers cannot be assumed.
Desired offline capabilities include:
- Local question answering.
- Local study knowledge search.
- Local speech recognition where supported.
- Local model inference.
- Local notes and study material.
- Offline quizzes / learning utilities where content is available.
- LAN communication with trusted nearby devices.

Cloud AI can enhance capability, but the StudyOS concept should remain useful without it.

5. AI / AGENT ROLES
-------------------
Historical role ideas include:
- Tutor: explains school subjects and learning material.
- Homework agent: helps interpret and work through assignments.
- Research agent: organizes and searches available knowledge/resources.
- Coding agent: assists with programming, debugging, and explanations.
- Study/planning agent: helps organize learning goals and sessions.

These roles should be orchestrated with clear permissions and must not be treated as autonomous authority over the user's device or accounts.

6. KNOWLEDGE AND MEMORY
-----------------------
StudyOS directions include local knowledge libraries, imported resources, retrieval/search, and persistent student context. RAG was discussed as a way to retrieve relevant local material before the AI answers. Memory and knowledge should remain separated conceptually:
- knowledge = reference material, school resources, imported documents;
- memory = user preferences/progress/context;
- model = reasoning/generation engine.

7. VOICE
--------
Voice direction includes local speech recognition through Whisper.cpp-style components and local/offline speech where practical. Voice is intended as an interface into tutoring, study control, and productivity rather than a requirement that every device always listen.

8. DEVICE / LAN INTEGRATION
---------------------------
The remote-brain concept allows StudyOS on a phone/watch/embedded device to ask an authorized stronger machine on the same trusted network to do heavier work. The design goal is local collaboration without forcing a public cloud dependency.

Important principles:
- explicit pairing/authorization;
- encrypted communication;
- clear device identity;
- revocable trust;
- local-first fallback;
- do not expose private study data to untrusted devices.

9. WEAR OS
----------
Wear OS direction includes lightweight study interactions such as tiles, quick status, reminders, timers, and sending small requests to the phone/remote brain. Heavy local LLM inference on a watch should be treated as hardware-dependent rather than assumed.

10. RELATIONSHIP TO CYBER PULSE
-------------------------------
StudyOS is strongly associated with Cyber Pulse's education/AI portfolio. DARTHWOLF / Ntsakiso Chauke is the primary documented builder and system architect in the available project history. No additional StudyOS-specific contributor role should be invented unless later records explicitly establish it.

11. RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER PROJECTS
----------------------------------
Evolution Learning influenced the structured-learning direction.
Study AI represents a more direct tutoring/education assistant.
StudyLock represents focus/security/family/teacher controls.
AEGIS and Infinity OS represent broader AI-computing, automation, device-control, security, and multi-agent directions that developed later.

12. DESIGN DIRECTION
--------------------
StudyOS belongs to the broader Cyber Pulse futuristic design family:
- dark/OLED interfaces;
- glass / depth;
- cyan, blue, purple neon language;
- clean study dashboards;
- strong visual hierarchy;
- smooth motion;
- AI-first command/learning surfaces.
StudyLock's yellow/orange liquid identity should not automatically be applied to StudyOS.

13. ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
--------------------------
- Offline-first, cloud optional.
- Modular model/runtime design.
- Hardware-aware model selection.
- Keep student data private by default.
- Explicit permissions for device-to-device actions.
- Separate model, memory, knowledge, and tools.
- Graceful fallback when a model or device is unavailable.
- Do not claim experimental features are complete until tested.
- Optimize for limited hardware and battery.

14. CURRENT KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY
------------------------------
The strongest confirmed StudyOS information is its offline-first v4 direction and expanded v5 Android/WearOS/embedded/distributed direction. Some deeper architecture concepts were experimental or planning-stage. Ember should answer using that distinction rather than converting every historical idea into a shipped feature.

================================================================================
END OF STUDYOS RECORD
